column1: # Starter manual table of resource-related GOVERNMENT REVENUE for source countries with no/thin EITI/GRD coverage.
# STARTER ESTIMATES — verify before relying on them; `confidence` flags how rough each is.
# Sources for every row are documented in docs/extractive/manual_resource_data_sources.md.
# total_resource_revenue_usd_bn = the source country's resource government revenue for that commodity-year
# frac_pre_profit / frac_post_profit / frac_equity sum to 1: pre = royalties/licence-fees/bonuses/production-entitlements (expensed
#   post = corporate income tax + special petroleum/mining taxes + windfall (the profit-based take); equity = state dividends / state-participation income.
# domestic_share = fraction attributed to the source country's own NOC/state firms (lands on the (parent==partner) CbCR cell);
#   the rest (1-domestic_share) is distributed to IOC HQ countries by hq_share_<commodity> in 1_8.

Ecuador oil & gas (state-dominated; service-contract model since ~2010). Total = SPNF 'ingresos petroleros'. pre = state crude export sales + sovereignty margin + royalties; post = SRI oil-sector taxes (CIT/withholding on hydrocarbons); equity = EP Petroecuador surplus + domestic-derivatives sales. NOTE: 2018-2020 use IMF 'oil revenue net of operational cost' (conservative); 2021-2022 use BCE gross 'ingresos petroleros' (not strictly comparable - gross 2018-20 ~ $11-12bn). EITI bilateral was broken/thin so this manual figure overrides it. Hand-collected 2026-06. Sources: BCE Informe Evolucion Economia 2022 Tabla 14; IMF Art IV CR21/228 & CR24/357; EITI Ecuador 2020-2022 Cuadros 37/39.
